cards.title: Strassen’s asymptotic rank conjecture for concise cubic tensors
cards.formal: For every n≥1 and every tensor T∈ℂ^n⊗ℂ^n⊗ℂ^n whose three flattenings all have rank n, is lim_{k→∞} R(T^⊗k)^(1/k)=n?
cards.definitions: R(T) is the least r such that T=Σ_{i=1}^r a_i⊗b_i⊗c_i with a_i,b_i,c_i∈ℂ^n. Each flattening views the tensor as a linear map from the dual of one factor into the tensor product of the other two. In T^⊗k the first, second and third tensor factors are respectively grouped, producing a tensor with three factors ℂ^(n^k). Submultiplicativity of rank makes the displayed limit equal to inf_{k≥1} R(T^⊗k)^(1/k). This is exact rank over ℂ, not border rank, and there is no explicitness or computational requirement on T.

context_blocks.text: Matrix rank has a simple algebraic characterization, whereas tensor rank changes substantially when many independent copies are considered jointly. Strassen’s conjecture says that in the asymptotic setting the three flattening dimensions already determine the answer.

The cubic concise formulation is the target proposed in the personal list. It includes matrix-multiplication tensors, so a positive resolution would imply matrix multiplication exponent two; the reverse implication is not claimed. The 2024–2026 source studies structural properties of asymptotic rank without proving this equality.

cards.definitions: For each n≥2, X={x₁,…,xₙ} and Y={y₁,…,yₙ} are disjoint alphabets of formal noncommuting variables. A noncommutative polynomial over F is a finite F-linear combination of words in those symbols; multiplication concatenates words and extends bilinearly, so variable order is part of a monomial. Pal_{n,n} has 2n variables, degree 2n and coefficients zero or one. A circuit is a finite acyclic graph whose leaves are variables or arbitrary constants from F and whose internal nodes are binary addition or binary multiplication gates. Multiplication inputs have a designated order. There is one output, fan-out is unrestricted, and the circuit must compute the formal polynomial exactly. Its size is the total number of nodes, as in the original paper. Division gates are not allowed; subtraction is available through the field constant −1. There is no bound on depth, intermediate polynomial degree, coefficient size or circuit uniformity. The syntactic degree of a variable leaf is one and of a constant leaf zero; an addition gate takes the maximum of its children’s syntactic degrees and a multiplication gate takes their sum. The circuit’s syntactic degree is their maximum over all nodes. A polynomial is homogeneous when every nonzero monomial has the same degree; the circuit need not have homogeneous intermediate outputs. The asymptotic claim means: for every fixed field F and every K>0, there is n₀(F,K) such that all n≥n₀ and all circuits computing Pal_{n,n} have more than Kn log₂n nodes. Explicitness is supplied by the displayed polynomial: a word’s coefficient is determined by checking its length, the two alphabets, and the reversed index sequence in time polynomial in n and the word length.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove or refute the displayed unrestricted-circuit lower bound beyond every constant multiple of n log n. Bounds only for formulas, homogeneous circuits or restricted syntactic degrees do not suffice. The accepted Raz theorem already proves this claim; a matching quadratic lower bound is stronger than the threshold originally asked for.

context_blocks.title: Multiplication remembers the order of operations
context_blocks.text: The monomials x₁x₂y₂y₁ and x₂x₁y₁y₂ are different formal words. In the palindrome polynomial, a sequence of x-indices is followed by the reversed sequence of y-indices. This supplies a concrete family in place of the original extraction’s phrase such lower bounds.

context_blocks.title: Intermediate computation was the missing freedom
context_blocks.text: A circuit may create high-degree terms that later cancel, even when its final output has modest degree. The earlier results restricted such intermediate behavior. The question was whether the lower-bound barrier could be passed while allowing every circuit in the model.

context_blocks.title: The original gap and the newer result
context_blocks.text: The source records a general Ω(n log n) bound and improves it under syntactic-degree restrictions. Raz’s accepted result gives Ω(n^(3/2)) for an explicit degree-proportional family and also applies to the palindrome target after identifying corresponding x and y variables. No extra restriction on the original circuit is needed.

context_blocks.title: How the theorem matches the palindrome target
context_blocks.text: Identifying yᵢ with xᵢ turns the polynomial into a one-alphabet palindrome of degree 2n. Its matrix of coefficients indexed by length-n prefixes and suffixes is a permutation matrix: a word occurs exactly when the suffix reverses the prefix. The matrix is full rank over every field, so Raz’s Theorem 1 supplies Ω((2n)√n) product gates. Variable identification cannot increase circuit size; hence this also lower-bounds circuits for the original two-alphabet polynomial.

context_blocks.title: A stronger concurrent statement is recorded separately

The monomials x₁x₂y₂y₁ and x₂x₁y₁y₂ are different formal words. In the palindrome polynomial, a sequence of x-indices is followed by the reversed sequence of y-indices. This supplies a concrete family in place of the original extraction’s phrase such lower bounds.

A circuit may create high-degree terms that later cancel, even when its final output has modest degree. The earlier results restricted such intermediate behavior. The question was whether the lower-bound barrier could be passed while allowing every circuit in the model.

The source records a general Ω(n log n) bound and improves it under syntactic-degree restrictions. Raz’s accepted result gives Ω(n^(3/2)) for an explicit degree-proportional family and also applies to the palindrome target after identifying corresponding x and y variables. No extra restriction on the original circuit is needed.

Identifying yᵢ with xᵢ turns the polynomial into a one-alphabet palindrome of degree 2n. Its matrix of coefficients indexed by length-n prefixes and suffixes is a permutation matrix: a word occurs exactly when the suffix reverses the prefix. The matrix is full rank over every field, so Raz’s Theorem 1 supplies Ω((2n)√n) product gates. Variable identification cannot increase circuit size; hence this also lower-bounds circuits for the original two-alphabet polynomial.

Shastri’s revised May preprint states a tight Ω(nd) bound for Pal_{n,d}, giving Ω(n²) when d=n. The card’s resolved n log n threshold does not depend on independently accepting that stronger proof: the accepted Raz result already crosses the required threshold.

cards.title: Exact generic subrank in arbitrary tensor formats
cards.formal: Historical question, resolved: for every algebraically closed field K, every tensor order k≥3 and all positive integers n₁,…,nₖ, determine the generic subrank Q_K(n₁,…,nₖ). Pielasa, Šafránek and Shatsila give the exact value min{n₁,…,nₖ,⌊(n₁+⋯+nₖ−(k−1))^{1/(k−1)}⌋}. Equivalently, it is the largest integer r≥1 satisfying r≤nᵢ for every i and r^{k−1}≤Σᵢnᵢ−(k−1). The formula includes both balanced and unbalanced formats.

cards.definitions: An algebraically closed field K is a field in which every nonconstant polynomial in one variable has a root. A tensor of format (n₁,…,nₖ) is an element T of K^{n₁}⊗⋯⊗K^{nₖ}, identified with its array of ∏ᵢnᵢ coefficients. For r≥1 let I_{r,k}=Σ_{j=1}^r e_j⊗⋯⊗e_j in (K^r)^{⊗k}, with k factors. The ordinary subrank Q_K(T) is the largest r for which there are K-linear maps Lᵢ:K^{nᵢ}→K^r satisfying (L₁⊗⋯⊗Lₖ)T=I_{r,k}; assign subrank zero to the zero tensor. The maps may be different in different factors and need not be invertible. A Zariski-closed set of tensors is a simultaneous zero set of polynomial equations in their coefficients, and a Zariski-open set is its complement. Generic subrank is the unique integer q such that Q_K(T)=q on some nonempty Zariski-open subset of the full tensor space. Such a subset exists in the source’s algebraically closed setting. The question concerns this generic value for each finite format, not the value on every tensor, the symmetric-tensor subspace, a limiting approximation to I_{r,k}, or tensor powers. All quantities and reductions are exact over K; no sampling distribution or numerical tolerance is used.
cards.answer_criterion: The published formula supplies the requested exact value for every format in the original algebraically closed setting, with matching generic upper and lower bounds. A generic lower bound alone or asymptotic equality would not have sufficed. Results about border subrank, asymptotic subrank or typical real subrank are different targets.
